To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1-cyclopentyl-1,4-pentadiene undergoes dimerization in the presence of nickel(0) to form the head-to-head type dimer, 4-cyclopentyle-1,5-heptadiene.

the nickel(0)-triphhenylphosphin catalyst dimerized 1-cyclopopyl-1,3 butadiene (1), and the dimer isolated in ca.50% was 2,4,4,8-tetra-2,6,6-trimethyl-4,6,8-undecatricene (2) in which the cyclopropan ring was incorporated in the molecule.

nickel(0)-triphhenylphosphane catalyzed dimerization of 1,3-butadiens, and that 1-cyclopenty-1,3 butadiene (1), which was used in the study, was converted to the head to head type dimer, 4-cyclopentyl-1,7-undecatetrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and study of the reactions of cyclopropyl-containing dienes.
the dimerization of cyclopropyl- and cyclobutylbutadienes.
the development of new synthetic methods for the construction of carbon-carbon bonds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nickel(0)-phosphine catalysis of 1 leads to the formation of a dimer with a head-to-head type of structure, and the cyclopropyl ring remains intact during the course of the reaction.
the nickel(0)-catalyzed dimerization of 1 proceeds via a 1,4-addition to form a nickel(II) complex followed by reductive elimination.
1-cyclobutyl-4,7,9,11-undecatetrane (3) was formed as a minor product, but the dimerization was predominantly head-to-head type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dimerization of 1 catalyzed by the nickel(0)-triphenylphosphine complex is the first successful example for the catalytic incorporation of the cyclopentane ring into the oligomers of 1.
the cyclopropyl group was incorporated into the dimeric products, and that the cyclopropanation occurred in the 1-position.
the dimer 4-cyclopentylidene-1,6-octadiene is formed from 1,3-butene by the catalytic effect of the nickel(0)-triphhenylphosphene complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cyclopropyl group can be used to control the stereochemistry of the dimer.
cyclopropane rings are not inert to the catalytic action by nickel(0)-phosphine complexes.
the cyclopropyl ring is incorporated in the dimeric product, which has not been observed before.
